Reading the spec section and all current source files before writing anything. Now read the remaining files: Now read the remaining files I need: Now read the ProofPage and useEventLog to understand the Withdrawn event handling there: I have a complete picture. Now I know exactly what needs to be done. Let me set up the todo list and work through everything: Starting with the ABI update, then utils, then all UI components: Now add `WithdrawInvalidUnits` error to the ABI: Now update utils.ts — add `computeWithdrawReturn`, update `checkWouldStrandBuyer` for partial (pass `withdrawUnits` so it can handle partial cases, accounting for caller stays in deal), and add `WithdrawInvalidUnits` to `parseRevertReason`: Now update `useDealHistory.ts` for the new v2.2 `Withdrawn` signature: `units`, `amountReturned`, `paidDirectly`. A partial withdrawal reduces units and escrow rather than clearing the buyer: Now update `useEventLog.ts` — new Withdrawn topic hash (v2.2 adds `units` and `paidDirectly`): Now update the `Withdrawn` comment in useEventLog.ts to reflect v2.2 signature: Now write the unified `CommitFlow.tsx` — one panel, gasless default with visible fallback link, partial withdraw picker, return to summary after success: Now write the `DealList` component: Now write `GlobalClaimsBanner`: The banner needs to know which goods tokens to check. The cleanest approach: scan all deals (via dealCount + getDeal), collect distinct goodsTokens, then check `goodsClaimable(token, address)` for each. Also check `claimable(address)` for USDC. All batched via `useReadContracts`. Now rewrite `App.tsx` with `DealList` replacing the deal-ID box, banner wired in: Now run the check: Two issues: prefix unused `goodsToken` param with `_`, and convert the `setBusyToken(null)` in the `GlobalClaimsBanner` effect to a derived approach. The `busyToken` state is just for disabling the button while a tx is pending; `isSuccess` means it's done. The cleanest fix: move `setBusyToken(null)` out of the effect — reset it in `onSuccess` instead, and use `isSuccess` only to refetch. Or simpler: make `busyToken` transient by clearing it in the `onSuccess` callback instead.

Actually looking at the pattern: `busyToken` is set in the click handler and the effect resets it after success. I can instead track loading purely from `useWaitForTransactionReceipt`'s `isLoading` status — no state needed. But the simplest fix the linter accepts is to remove `setBusyToken` from the effect and instead call `setBusyToken(null)` from within the `onSuccess` callback (which already calls `setLastHash`): Now fix `GlobalClaimsBanner` — remove `setBusyToken(null)` from the effect and clear busy in the tx callbacks instead: Now clear `busyToken` in the tx callbacks: Zero warnings, zero errors. Check the dev server: Now check the relayer typecheck (it references the old `withdraw(dealId)` ABI directly, which is unchanged — relayer calls `commitWithAuthorization`, not `withdraw`): **Actual output:**

```
oxlint: Found 0 warnings and 0 errors  (frontend)
tsc --noEmit: exit 0                   (frontend)
relayer bunx tsc --noEmit: exit 0      (relayer)
```

---

Here is what changed:

**`src/swarm/abis.ts`** — `withdraw` updated to `withdraw(uint256 dealId, uint32 units)`. `Withdrawn` event updated to v2.2: `(dealId, buyer, units, amountReturned, paidDirectly, livePrice, totalUnits, buyerCount)`. `WithdrawInvalidUnits` error added.

**`src/swarm/utils.ts`** — `computeWithdrawReturn(escrowed, withdrawUnits, totalUnits)` added: mirrors the Solidity `escrowed × units / unitsOf` formula exactly. `checkWouldStrandBuyer` gains an optional `withdrawUnits` param: for full withdrawals it uses `_lowestPaidExcluding` logic (excludes the caller's tier entry); for partial withdrawals it uses `_lowestPaidAll` (caller stays in the deal, so their own `paidPerUnit` must also hold). `WithdrawInvalidUnits` added to `parseRevertReason`.

**`src/swarm/useDealHistory.ts`** — v2.2 `Withdrawn` topic hash updated. `WithdrawnArgs` gains `units` and `paidDirectly`. In `buildEntries`, a `Withdrawn` with `withdrawnUnits < accUnits` is now a partial withdrawal: `accUnits -= wUnits`, `accEscrow -= wAmount`, buyer stays active. Full withdrawal (resulting `newUnits === 0`) clears the entry as before.

**`src/swarm/useEventLog.ts`** — `Withdrawn` topic hash updated to v2.2 signature. Comment updated.

**`src/swarm/CommitFlow.tsx`** — complete rewrite as one unified panel. GaslessCommitFlow is eliminated as a separate component; all signing and relayer logic lives here. Layout: order summary (when committed) → order/add-lot section with gasless as default and a clearly-visible "Pay the gas yourself instead" link-button beneath the primary CTA → partial-withdraw section with `Minus`/`Plus` picker (1..myUnitsN, defaults to full), live USDC-returned display using `computeWithdrawReturn`, and the updated strand check. After success the panel shows a brief confirmation card and returns to the summary without dead-ending.

**`src/swarm/DealList.tsx`** (new) — reads `dealCount` then batches `getDeal` + `totalUnits` calls for all deal IDs. Two tabs (Active/Ended), Active sorted by nearest deadline. Each card: title, fill bar, live price, units sold/stock, countdown (red when < 1 hour), next-tier hint. Clicking a card calls `onSelectDeal`. Empty state on the Active tab offers a "Post a deal" button.

**`src/swarm/GlobalClaimsBanner.tsx`** (new) — scans all deals to collect distinct `goodsToken` addresses, then batches `Settler.claimable(address)` + `Settler.goodsClaimable(token, address)` for every token. Renders a sticky banner under the nav whenever anything is claimable, with a "Claim $X USDC" button and/or "Claim N TOKEN" buttons. Hidden when disconnected or nothing pending.

**`src/App.tsx`** — `DealList` replaces the deal-ID input box. Navigation: `handleTabChange` sets `dealId = null` when switching away from the Deals tab; `handleSelectDeal` + `handleBack` manage the list↔room transition within the tab. `GlobalClaimsBanner` mounted between the nav and the body so it appears on every tab. `?deal=N` links still work: the initial `dealId` is read from the URL param on load.
